reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference-class anchor: a one-month-ahead Tokyo all-items YoY forecast should start from persistence around the latest official monthly cluster rather than from a fresh trend break. The recent public official context is 2.9, 2.9, 3.5, and 3.4 percent through May, and the June database update confirms the target table is current for the next release cycle.

Level and momentum split: the level is high by Japan's pre-2022 standards but stable within the recent 2.9 to 3.5 percent band. Momentum from March to May was upward then flat, so I avoid extrapolating another large rise but keep the center above 3 percent.

Mechanism split: food and rice inflation keep an upside tail in all-items CPI, while energy and utility subsidy timing can pull the annual rate down. Services persistence supports the center, but fresh-food volatility argues against a narrow interval.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior from recent official Tokyo all-items YoY prints uses a short-sample average of Feb-May 2026: (2.9 + 2.9 + 3.5 + 3.4) / 4 = 3.175. I round the prior center to 3.2, add +0.1 for sticky food/services pressure, and make no additional June-catalog-estimate adjustment, giving 3.3. For the 80% interval, recent first-print dispersion spans 0.6 percentage points, but headline energy/fresh-food risk and the small sample justify about +/-0.8 around the point, giving 2.5 to 4.1.

Counter-consideration and scenarios: downside outside the interval would come from a sharp energy-subsidy or gasoline-base-effect drop plus softer fresh food, pushing the July print below 2.5. Upside outside the interval would require renewed rice/food acceleration or utility pass-through pushing above 4.1. The central case is persistence near the low-to-mid 3 percent range.
